reduced competition between task-appropriate actions in limb aprraxia is evident when actions are associated with single tools (e.g., grasp-on-use conflict) and when actions are associated within a pair of similar tools (e.g, reduced neighborhood effects).
reduced ability of tool use actions to inhibit competing task-inappropriate representations is evident in both single-tool and between-tool competition tasks.

patients with left hemisphere stroke (LHS) and limb apraxia have reduced ability to activate appropriate tool use actions and to compete between tool use actions when there is competition within single tools (e.g., a corkscrew that requires a grasp-on-use action) as well as when there is competition between tool use actions (e.g., between a hammer and a screwdriver).

the left inferior frontal cortex, which is known to be important in tool use, is important for both the selection of the correct tool action and the suppression of competing actions.

The main takeaway from our work is that

apraxic patients with left hemisphere damage show reduced ability to compete between tool actions that are associated with a single tool (grasp-on-tool conflict) as well a reduced ability to compete across tools (neighborhood effects).
reduced competition within and between tool actions is a core deficit of limb apraxia.
the left hemisphere plays a key role in resolving conflict in the selection of tool-related actions, and that this process is disrupted in patients with limb aprraxia.
